translation:
_Kaam kaso je machh kachh hove, shankhasur na vidare.
O pratipal saphalmein vyapak, kahahu konaku maare. ||2||_
(What need was there for Him to become a fish or a tortoise, or to slay Shankhasura? He who pervades all and sustains everyone as protector — tell me, who could ever slay Him?)

_Hari varaah bhayo nahin kabahun, dashan bhavan dhaari.
O to kaam nahin Ramke, jhunth kahai sansari. ||3||_
(Hari never once became a boar bearing the earth upon his tusks — that is not the work of Ram; worldly people speak falsehood.)

_O nahin Ram khambh jine phaara, Prahlad nahin re ugaarya.
O nirgun sabanse nyaara, nahin jeeta nahin haara. ||4||_
(It was not Ram who split open the pillar and rescued Prahlad. He, the attributeless one, stands apart from all, wholly different — He has never won nor lost.)

_Baaman hoi Bal nahin jaacha, jo jaachai so maaya.
O alekh lekhme nahin, o kaahu gaya na aaya. ||5||_
(He did not become a dwarf and beg from King Bali — whoever begs is bound by maya. He, the unaccountable one, is beyond all reckoning; He has never gone anywhere nor come from anywhere.)

_Parshuram hoi prithvi nahin deeni, kshatri koi na santaapya.
Bin bichaar sakal jug bhoola, maaye jug bharmaya. ||6||_
(He did not become Parshuram and give away the earth, nor did He torment any Kshatriya. Without reflection the whole age has gone astray — maya has deluded the age.)

_Sirajanhaar Sita nahi varne, jal paashaan nahin baandhe.
O Raam karta kar bujhe, (jo sumre) so aandhe. ||7||_
(The Creator did not marry Sita, nor did He bind stones upon water. Whoever takes Ram the Creator to be a mere doer (whoever remembers Him thus) is blind.)

_Karta Kahaan nahin re Gokul, karto Kans na maare.
O akal niranjan kala nahi kabahu, sab kachhu unke saare. ||8||_
(The Creator did not become Krishna in Gokul, nor did He slay Kansa. He, the unfathomable, stainless one, never took such a form — everything is His own arrangement.)

_Aisa samrath sab kaahu kiya, kari kari raha lokaanna.
Jal thal jeev sakalme vyaapak, aisa hai vardaana. ||9||_
(Such a Mighty One has made all of this and keeps sustaining the worlds; He pervades every being in water and on land — such is His boon.)

_Dash avataar ishwari maaya, taako karta kar boojha.
Kahat Kabir Raam avinaashi, aave jaaye so dooja. ||10||_
(The ten avatars are the Lord's own divine maya — do not take them for the Creator Himself. Kabir says: Ram is imperishable; whatever comes and goes is something other than Him.)

Das Kabirji says: O saints, whatever comes and goes is Maya-Brahm. That Purna-Brahm, the Parabrahm, no one has ever been able to fathom or estimate. That Parabrahm neither goes anywhere nor is given away by anyone. What need did this Parabrahm have to take the form of a fish or a tortoise avatar? He did not slay Shankhasura. Pervading everything, He is the Protector who nourishes and sustains all — tell me, then, who could possibly kill Him or destroy Him? This Lord never became a boar, nor did He bear the earth on His tusks. Worldly people lay this blame on Him, for such a deed is not the work of Lord Ram. This Lord Ram did not split open the pillar, nor did He rescue Prahlad. He is free of the three gunas, wholly set apart from everyone, entirely different — He has never known success or failure, has never won or lost. He did not go and beg deceitfully before King Bali — that is not the Lord's doing, that is the work of maya. He is unknowable, has never become something that can be known; He has never, in any age, gone anywhere or come from anywhere. Taking the form of Parshuram, He did not give the earth to anyone, nor did He torment any Kshatriya. Creator of the universe though Lord Ram is, if one takes Him — because of such deeds performed in avatar form — to be merely an avatar-being (avatari), and worships and serves the avatars as such, [that is a mistake, for] He whom none has ever fathomed or understood, who is free of all attachment — it is on Him alone that this whole world depends. Such a Mighty, All-Powerful Lord has fashioned, and keeps fashioning, all these twenty-one universes and fourteen worlds, and keeps them running; He pervades water, land, and everything else — such is that All-Powerful, All-Giving Lord. The ten avatars are His own wondrous, divine maya; people take these avatars to be the Creator-Lord of the world, but the Transcendent Ram, who never perishes, never comes or goes anywhere at any time — He is unmoving.

In the Samagam, the Bijak's very first rameni [devotional song] has been placed as the opening rameni, on the theme of the wish-born feminine avatar; and midway through the Samagam, the 8th rameni given is the one on the theme "Saints, whatever comes and goes is maya." But compared with the published Bijak texts, there is a slight difference of reading in these Samagam renenis — so the seventh line of this rameni differs somewhat in other Bijak texts. There it reads:

_Vai Raghunath ek kai sumire, jo sumirai so andha. ||7||_
(Whoever remembers Raghunath alone — whoever remembers thus is blind.)

In support of these words, the Bijak texts write that those who understand the Lord and Ram in this way [merely as an avatar-doer] are blind, without understanding. In the Samagam this seventh line reads instead:

_O Raam karta kar boojhe (jo samre) so andha._
(Whoever takes Ram the Creator to be understood as a mere doer — whoever remembers Him thus — is blind.)

People count Lord Ram and Krishna among the ten avatars and refer to them as "avatari" [avatar-beings], but there is no need to count this Ram and Krishna merely as avataris. What is said about Ram through Kabir's sakhi on page 98 of the printed Samagam we shall discuss in that chapter; but Kabirwani, Year 1, Issue 11, page 5, clarifies about this Ram as follows:

"In the above words of Kabir Sahib, in the passage where it says 'vai Raghunath ek hai sumire so andha' [whoever remembers Raghunath alone is blind], those who recall the name of Ram are called blind, that is, unwise. This statement causes distress to those who hold the incarnate Lord Ram to be the Supreme Being, and to Sadguru Kabir's own guru, Shri Ramanand Swami, and to the other great souls among his followers — but it is not the way of great souls to cause distress to anyone's heart. A great soul such as Sadguru Kabir Sahib would not call his own guru and his followers unwise. This compels one to the conclusion that this line must be an interpolation. Kabir himself says: 'aape guru kriya kichhu keenho, nirgun chalakh lakhaai; sahaj samadhi unmuni jaage, sahaj milai saguraai' (the Guru himself performed some act, revealing a glimpse of the attributeless; through it the natural samadhi awakens in the mind beyond mind, and the true guru's grace is met with ease) — from these words it follows that Kabirji was Ramchandra's supreme devotee and worshipper. Having seen Kabirji's statements refuting the avatars, some commentators, worshippers, and scholars say that Kabirji also carried Muslim cultural influences. But looking at the actual words themselves, these scholars' claims appear false. Since the Bijak is a compiled text, differences of a line or two, and variant readings, are found among its different manuscript copies."

In the Samagam, in the given Shabda (Word) 8, "Saints, whatever comes and goes is maya," it is said that whoever remembers Ram [in that framework] is blind, without understanding — and this controversial statement has been read as showing opposition to devotion to Ram. To counter this, [commentators] argue, using the words found in Shabda 4, Kabirwani Year 1, Issue 11, page 5, that Kabirji was in fact a supporter of devotion to Ram; and accordingly it is stated so also in the Samagam of Vasana and elsewhere; and in the Bijak, under "Aspashta" [the unclear/obscure section], Shabda 5, one finds "see the explanation" — and on this basis it is claimed that Kabirji's assent to devotion to Ram has been established. The words of Shabda 4, beginning "aape guru kripa keenhi" [you, the guru, showed grace], occur as Shabda 7 or in some such order in other Bijak texts — but the line containing these words actually belongs to the Shabda that begins "santo kahi to ko patipai" [O saints, tell me, who then attains the Lord]. In this way, devout people have sought to prove that Kabir accepted devotion to Ram. Kabir did not accept the ten avatars, however — there is another verse [pad] on this too. In Grantha-18, page 118, there is a rameni.

|| Rameni ||

_Niraakaar nirgun nahin paaya, parathamai ekahi aapai aapa. ||1||_
(The formless, attributeless one could not be found — in the very beginning, He alone existed, by Himself.)

_Tab nahin pavan aakaasa, tab nahin chand sooraj parakaaya. ||2||_
(Then there was no wind, no sky; then there was no light of moon or sun, no embodied form.)

_Tab nahin paanch tattva gun teeni, tab nahin maaya srishtaj keeni. ||3||_
(Then there were no five elements, no three gunas; then maya had not fashioned creation.)

_Tab nahin sargun sakal pasaara, tab nahin keene dasau avataara. ||4||_
(Then there was no manifest expanse of qualities at all; then the ten avatars had not been taken.)

_Tab nahin machh kachh aur vaaraaha, tab nahin Narsimha Harnaakansh maara. ||5||_
(Then there was no fish, no tortoise, no boar; then Hiranyakashipu had not been slain as Narsimha.)

_Tab nahin Krishna Kans Bal Baavan, tab nahin Raghupati tab nahin Raavan. ||6||_
(Then there was no Krishna, no Kansa, no Bali, no Vaman; then there was no Raghupati [Ram], and no Ravan.)

_Tab nahin shruti Ved Puraan, tab nahin Kaazi Kiteb Kuraana. ||7||_
(Then there were no Shrutis, no Vedas, no Puranas; then there was no Qazi, no scripture, no Quran.)

_Tab nahin saayet saat taranga, tab nahin Sarasvati Jamuna Ganga. ||8||_
(Then there were no waves upon the seven seas; then there was no Sarasvati, Yamuna, or Ganga.)

_Tab nahin paap dharam guru shishya, tab nahin pathan gunanka lekh. ||9||_
(Then there was no sin or virtue, no guru or disciple; then there was no reading, counting, or writing.)

_Tab nahin jog jagan vrat pooja, tab nahin devi daiv nahin dooja. ||10||_
(Then there was no yoga, yajna, vow, or worship; then there was no goddess, no deity, nothing else.)

|| Sakhi ||

_Kahe Kabir vichaareekai, tab ek kartap naahin.
Param purush aapai hutai, agam agochar maanhi._
(Kabir says, having reflected: at that time not even a single act was being done. The Supreme Being alone existed by Himself, within the unapproachable, imperceptible reality.)

_Agam agochar gam nahin, jahaan jhilmil jot.
Tahaan Kabira bandagi, paata punna nahi chhot._
(Where that unapproachable, imperceptible one cannot be reached, where there is only a shimmering radiance — there, says Kabira, is true worship; there, no gain of merit and no touch of sin remain.)

Das Kabirji says: when in the world there was not yet anything like the Brahm-tattva that transcends the three gunas, at that very first moment only You, the Parabrahm Parmatma, existed. Then there was no wind or sky; then there was no light of moon or sun; then there were no five elements and three gunas; then there was neither creation nor maya. Then nothing pervaded everywhere in manifest, embodied form; then the ten avatars had not been taken. Then Ram was not fish, tortoise, or boar; then Hiranyakashipu had not been slain in the form of Narsimha; then Krishna had not slain Kansa. Then there was no Ram, no Ravan. Then there were no Shrutis, Vedas, Puranas. Then there was no Qazi, no scripture, no Quran; then there were no waves upon the seven oceans. Then there was no triveni confluence of Sarasvati, Yamuna, and Ganga. Then there was no sin or virtue, no guru or disciple; then there was no reckoning of learning and counting. Then there was no yoga, yajna, vow, or worship; then there was no god, goddess, or anything else.

The Broken Raas — The Raas Faltered

While discussing exclusive devotion (ananya bhakti), it is said that Gopaldas dispelled the confusion about whether the Supreme Being's form is with-form (sakar) or formless (nirakar) by declaring that the Lord's true nature is beyond the form-endowed divine essence in which He manifests through the ten avatars — and thereby the chapter has been opened on the Complete Parabrahm Parmatma whom we are to worship. That supreme reality which is the meeting-point of the named-and-formed and the nameless-formless, of sagun and nirgun — the flute-charmer Morli Manohar — is like the water held in Radha's hands; the waves that arise in that water are the avatars. Just as those waves break and dissolve, so the avatars come to an end. But it is the essence of the flute-charmer Himself — the unmoving Parabrahm, Shri Krishna-Ram, who is beyond all avatars — whom it has been resolved to worship. For the sake of His devotees the Lord comes. [Now] the raas faltered, and something went amiss.

It came to a halt; a break occurred.

_Bhagat manorath Jivana, main dhar kroti avataar.
Ek daski kaha chali, jo bhagat mohe praan aadhaar._
(For the sake of My devotees' heartfelt wishes, O Jivana, I would take on a crore of avatars. What then is the mere talk of ten? — for My devotees are the very support of My life-breath.)

Maharaj Jivandasji says: the Lord says, "For the sake of My devotees' wishes and desires I am ready to take avatar a crore times over — so what wonder is there in speaking of only ten avatars? For My devotees are exceedingly dear to Me."

The Lord's raas-lila is unbroken (akhand) — it does not cease even for as long as it takes to close and open one's eyes; that is, this divine play is never interrupted. In support of this, the words of Hit Harivanshji are given.

_Saamaane saam jhulaavat jhoole Jamunaaki teer,
sadaa vasant hot Vrindaavan rachyo Hit Harivansh bal bheerye._
(Facing one another, they swing upon the swing on the bank of the Yamuna; it is ever springtime in Vrindavan — so has Hit Harivansh, filled with fervor, described it.)

Hit Harivansh says: on the banks of the Yamuna, upon a swing, Lord Krishna swings Radhaji. Thus in Vrindavan there is always joy and delight as of a spring festival; the raas enacted there fills Hit Harivansh with delight. Since the raas is unbroken, there is no need to think, on the notion of the ten avatars, that the Lord manifests in various forms and then dissolves away. Rather, the Lord takes avatar for the sake of His devotees. About what happened when the Lord's raas was broken, Kabirji says:

_Kabir Ved bada na vedasi, nahin Gokulki vrajanaar.
Unhe sahaj na paai, rahi pokaar pokaar. ||1||_
(Kabir says: the Veda is not great enough for this truth, nor are the Braj-women of Gokul great enough — they could not attain that natural union with ease, and were left crying out in lament.)

Das Kabirji says: to attain the essence and mystery of the Lord's love, the Veda itself, however great, is not sufficient; nor can even those who know the Veda attain, or help others attain, this supreme reality. Nor is the stature of the Braj-women of Gokul so great, for they could not easily and simply attain the full bliss of that love; so when the circle of the raas broke, they became distressed and agitated, crying out to the Lord in the pain of separation.

_Prem na peeno Gopika, kachhuk shank rahi man maanhi.
Sur muni dekhan lage Jivana, varti taaki chhaanhi. ||2||_
(The gopis did not fully drink of that love — a trace of doubt remained in their minds. O Jivana, when the gods and sages began to watch, its shadow-influence fell upon them.)

Maharaj Jivandasji says: the gopis could not fully attain the joy of love in the raas-lila, because a slight trace of pride still lingered within them — for the gods and sages watched their sport, and the influence of being so watched fell upon their minds, and so the raas was broken.

Vrindavan's swans, chakoras, chatakas, cuckoos, trees, creepers, vines, the multitude of flowers, the cows, calves, cowherds, gopis, and the playful sport of the gracious Lord — all of this is unbroken (akhand). At the end of the cosmic cycle, the five elements, the three gunas, and the fourteen worlds are dissolved, but Vrindavan remains unbroken. Even at the end of the cycle, not a single leaf falls from the flute-bearer's tree of this forest. Only where time and maya have influence does dissolution occur. But in Vrindavan there is the Lord's own maya, His own tenderness — the tenderness of love, the tenderness of love. The raas was broken, yet Kabirji offers this counsel to the gopis:

_Kabir sahaj ma chhaandes sundari, tumhe sahajanandaki aan.
Tan jaataan jo pan rahai, to nirbhe gade nishaan._
(Kabir says: O beautiful ones, do not abandon your natural state; you are bound by the vow of natural bliss. Even if the body should perish, if your resolve remains, then you shall plant your victory-banner fearlessly.)

Das Kabirji says: O beautiful gopis! Do not abandon your natural state (sahajavastha); do not abandon your undistorted state. You have been enjoined to hold to the undistorted state of Prem-Lakshana Bhakti [love-natured devotion] to the Lord. So even if your body should perish, if your resolve is preserved, do not concern yourselves with the body; by doing so you shall fearlessly sound the drum of your victory.

_Kabir trigun rahit Kahaanuo, jine rachyo akhandit raas.
Prem jot Braj sundari, tahaan baare maas vilaas._
(Kabir says: this Krishna, free of the three gunas, has fashioned the unbroken raas; the beauties of Braj are like flames of love — there, delight goes on through all twelve months of the year.)

Das Kabirji says: this Lord Krishna is beyond the three gunas — He who has fashioned this unbroken raas. The beauties of Braj are like the flame of Prem-Lakshana Bhakti; and so in Vrindavan, joy and delight continue unbroken through all twelve months.

Through lines from a kirtan of Maharaj Adhyaruji, this raas has been described:

_Mor peench Chandra mugar sir sohe, nij maaya dev tribhovan sohe.
Sohe gunjaakal haaro, Hari Hari._
(The peacock-feather crest with its moon-mark adorns His head; through His own maya, the Lord adorns all three worlds. The garland of gunja-berries adorns Him — Hari, Hari!)

In Lord Krishna's crown, the moon-shaped crest of peacock feathers shines; such is the Lord who, through His own maya, shines throughout all three worlds. Around His neck shines a garland of gunja-berries.

In this way, while the Lord was playing the raas, the gods and sages came rushing to watch, and began hailing Him with cries of victory, showering flowers upon Him. They said:

_Dhan dhan Gokulani Brijnaare, kun punya keedhalaan re.
Dhan dhan Gokulani Brijnaar._
(Blessed, blessed are the Braj-women of Gokul — what merit must they have earned! Blessed, blessed are the Braj-women of Gokul.)

"Blessed, blessed are the women of Gokul — what merit they must have earned, that they get to play such a raas! Blessed, blessed are these women of Gokul" — the gods praised them thus, and because of this praise a feeling of self-importance, of being especially fortunate, arose in the gopis' minds. But this feeling did not arise in Radhaji, and so the Lord went into hiding (antardhyan) together with Radhaji. Jivandasji said: "Brothers, true love was pointlessly interrupted, so that it became as if it had never happened, because of separation from the Lord." If even a shadow of wickedness touches it, then even true love becomes false; therefore one should set aside distortion and love the Lord without any desire for reward. Again, he gave a second sakhi:

_Prem na peeno Gopika, kachhuk shank rahi man maanhi.
Sur muni dekhan lage Jivana, varti taaki chhaanhi. ||1||_
(The gopis did not fully drink of that love — a trace of doubt remained in their minds. O Jivana, when the gods and sages began to watch, its shadow-influence fell upon them.)

The shadow of beings such as the gods and sages is called the shadow of the wicked, because the gods are given to pleasure and the sages are worshippers of the gods, so both are counted alike in this. The meaning of the "shadow of the wicked" is this: if one holds supreme, exclusive devotion (para-bhakti, ananya-bhakti) toward Krishna, then one's attention should not turn toward gods or worldly people. Radhaji had such love for the Lord that He took her along with Him as He disappeared, but even she was touched by this influence of wickedness — the feeling arose in her, "I am supremely fortunate, since the Lord keeps me with Him and has become invisible" — and so, while He was carrying Radhaji along, the Lord said, "if you cling to the branch of a tree, I will change My shoulder"; and having said this, He left her hanging from the branch of a tree and Himself vanished. Thus Radhaji's plight became even worse than that of the other gopis. All the gopis gathered together, and, filled with regret, said, "the raas was pointlessly interrupted." Thus even a subtle trace of ego creates a disturbance in devotion.

_Khoji aap saraahataan, teen baatki dhaat.
Budh ochhi vaachaa akal, aavaradaa ghat jaat._
(Khoji says: in praising oneself, three things suffer harm — one's intellect diminishes, one's speech becomes foolish, and one's lifespan grows shorter.)

Maharaj Khojiji says: from self-praise — praising oneself — we suffer harm in three respects: our intellect diminishes, our speech becomes a laughingstock, and our lifespan is shortened.

_Sumirat jinke charanko, moh jaat hai bhaag.
Nirmohi vah hoy to, kaa acharajki baat._
(By remembering whose feet, delusion flees away — if He Himself is free of delusion, what wonder is there in that?)

_Mohi Dashrath Laal hai, nirmohi Nandlaal.
Ve ban ban dhoondhat phire, inhi taaji Braj baal._
(Dashrath's son [Ram] was bound by delusion; Nandlal [Krishna] is free of delusion. He wandered from forest to forest searching, while He at once left behind the young women of Braj.)

By remembering whose feet our delusion departs — if such a Lord is Himself free of delusion and desire, what wonder is there in that? Ram, the son of Dashrath, was bound by delusion; Krishna was free of delusion. Ram wandered through forest after forest searching for Sita, whereas Shri Krishna simply left the gopis of Braj behind.

|| The Unbroken Raas: The Natural Certainty of the Lover — Master of the Court and Master of the Chamber ||
|| The Unbroken Raas: The Highest Culmination of Love-Devotion ||
|| The Unbroken Raas: The Natural Certainty of the Lover — Master of the Court and Master of the Chamber ||

_Prem bhakti ekai palak, kohi varasko yog.
Prem bhakti sab yog hai, yog prem bivan rog._
(One single moment of love-devotion is worth more than the yoga of countless years. Love-devotion is itself the complete yoga, while yoga without love is merely a disease.)

Even if love-natured devotion (prem-lakshana bhakti) lasts for only a single moment, it is greater than crores of years of yogic practice. Love-devotion is in itself the complete yoga, whereas yoga practiced without love, practiced only for show, is like a disease that neither kills nor lets one grow — it is merely painful, like an affliction.

To support the view that the raas is regarded as unbroken, a pad of Narsinh Mehta is given.

|| Raag Kedaro ||

_Shaamloji sukhanu nidhaan re sajani.
Ven vaahine vahaale tedi ramaadyaan, dei karkalade maan re sajani. ||tek|| ||1||
Raam ramataan sukhad mohyaa, muniji bhoolyaa dhyaan re sajani.
Paamyaa mahaaras amo raakhi nav jaanyo, kaain ek keedhun maan re sajani. ||2||
Mananu kaaran Mohan jaane, Hari thayaa antardhyaan re sajani.
Beh vachan bole re Vraj vanitaa, kaahu nav deethaa Kahaan re sajani. ||3||
Vyaaku thai re Vrindaavan shodhyaa,
Aatur thai antargat joyun, madhyathi pragatyaa Kahaan re sajani.
Narsaiyaachaa swaami bhale malyaa, paamyaa param nidhaan re sajani. ||4||_
(O friend, Shyamji is a treasure-house of bliss. Playing His flute, the Beloved called us and made us dance the raas, honoring us by holding our hands, O friend. Playing with Him we were enchanted by that bliss, and even the sages forgot their meditation. We attained the supreme essence of love, but did not recognize You for who You were, O friend, and let a little pride arise. Mohan knew what was in our minds, and Hari became hidden. The women of Braj spoke words of anguish, saying, 'We can nowhere see Kahan.' Distressed, we searched all through Vrindavan; eager, we looked within, and from our very midst Kahan appeared. Narsaiya's Lord has been graciously met — we have attained the supreme treasure.)

O friend, Lord Krishna is the treasure-house that bestows supreme bliss. O friend, the beloved Lord played His flute and called us, welcoming and honoring us with a gentle smile, and made us play the raas — and even the sages forgot to meditate. O friend, we attained the supreme essence of love, but we could not fully understand You, and some pride arose within us. O friend, Lord Krishna came to know of the pride that lay in our minds, and so the Lord became hidden. O friend, and so the gopis of Braj, overwhelmed by separation, began to utter words of lament. Becoming distraught, they searched throughout Vrindavan but could nowhere see the Lord. O friend, then, restless and anguished, they looked within themselves, and there they found the Lord, like a treasure of supreme love and bliss.

In this chapter on the Unbroken [Raas], the highest culmination of love-devotion has been shown. The unbrokenness of the raas has been examined. It has been raised for consideration: the Lord manifested from the midst of the gopis — how and why did He manifest, and where did He become hidden? Everyone says the raas faltered, that a flaw came upon it, an obstruction arose, it went wrong, a delay occurred — so then how did the raas come to be called unbroken? This confusion has been resolved, and to show that the raas is indeed unbroken and never truly breaks, Narsinh Mehta's pad in the Sindhuda raga has been given.

|| Ram Sindhuko ||

_Jeere dhanya tun dhanya tun em kahai Shri Hari, Narsinho maaro bhakt saacho.
Mooki purushaatan sakhi re veshe thayo, taahraa premthi hun re naachyo. ||1||
Jeere mujmaan tujmaan bhed nahin naagaraa, maan maari tun ved vaani.
Haju tujne prateet na upaje, mokalyun mein tune taadhu paani. ||2||
Jeere mosaalun karyun kaan-e visar, tujne haar aapyo pratyaksh bhoop.
Chaud lokmaan maare duj samo ko nahin, taaheru maaher ek roop. ||3||
Jeere tohro akshar saambhale gaaye, tehnaa kul sahit paavan thaaye.
Bhaage Narsinh-o meethaan boli shun reejhavo, taare kar jodi Krishnaji sam khaaye. ||4||_
('Oh, blessed are you, blessed are you,' says Shri Hari: 'Narsinh is My true devotee. Setting aside your manhood, you took the form and disposition of a sakhi; out of love for you, I too danced.' 'There is no difference between you and Me, O clever one; take My word as truly as scripture. If you still have no faith in this, know that I sent you the cold water Myself.' 'Why do you forget the gift-ceremony I performed for you — I Myself, in visible form as king, gave you the garland. In all fourteen worlds there is no one else like you to Me; your honor is unique.' 'Whoever hears and sings your composition becomes purified, together with his whole family.' Narsinh says: 'Why do You please me with such sweet words?' — and then, folding his hands, Krishnaji swore that it was so.)

'Well done!' says the Lord, 'blessed are you, blessed are you, O Narsinh! You are My true devotee. You set aside your manhood and took on the disposition of a sakhi, and out of love for you I acted just as you said. O clever one, there is no difference between Me and you — believe that this true, well-founded statement of Mine is correct. Do you still not feel assured? It was I Myself who sent you the cold water. It was I Myself who performed your gift-ceremony and gave you the garland in the very presence of King Ramandalik. In all fourteen worlds there is no one else like you to Me. My form and your form are one and the same. Whoever sings and hears your bhajans and kirtans becomes purified, together with his whole family.' Narsinh Mehta says, 'O Lord, why do You please me with such sweet, sweet words?' — at that, the Lord, agreeing wholeheartedly, folded his hands and, with an oath, said, 'Truly, I regard you as My true devotee.'

In Patra Bhagwan Bapu, Grantha No. 1, page 60, Pad 130, of the Haarmala, there is a pad of similar sentiment.

|| Kadarja Sindhuko ||

_Jeere dhanya tun dhanya tun em kahe Shri Hari, trigun rahit mohyun man maaru.
Trigun rahit man thayun taaru.
Jeere kot brahmaandpati karahun vinati, pooran mune hridayaamaan dhyaan taaru. ||tek||
Narsaiya tun vachan maan maaru.
Jeere Brahma Shankar Sati (Shruti) Sanakaadik aade jati, Shesh Mahesh (Shuk) ghare dhyaan maaru.
Man karm vachne vare mugatne anusare, evi mugati taare charane vaaru. ||1||
Maare jevi Vraj sundari tevo j Narsaiyo, ene niramal mane maaro jas gaayo.
Rank hun ank bhari urpar raakhio, jem kusumni paankhadi heet saahyo. ||2||
Jeere kunj leelaae tun madhukar maahvaa, purush naame koi paas aave.
Aade tahaan Shri Hari Brij vanitaa khari, tahaan Narsaiyo charanni rog naahe. ||3||
Narsaiya vinaa mune kon ladaave._
('Blessed are you, blessed are you,' says Shri Hari, 'even though I am beyond the three gunas, My mind has been drawn to you; your mind too has become free of the three gunas. I, the Lord of countless universes, entreat you: My complete meditation is fixed within your heart. Narsinh, accept these words of Mine as true. Brahma, Shankar, the Shrutis, Sanaka and the other primal ascetics, Shesh, Mahesh, and Shukdev all keep their meditation fixed on Me. Whatever liberation people seek through mind, deed, and word — that liberation I offer freely at your feet.' 'Just as dear to Me as the beauties of Braj is Narsinh himself, who with a pure mind has sung My praise. Though I am humble, I have been held close to your bosom, as a flower holds its petals close.' 'In the playful groves you are like a honey-drinking bee; only one who has cast off manhood can come near. There truly reside the wives of Braj, devoted to Shri Hari; there, at Narsinh's feet, no ailment of separation remains. Without Narsinh, who else would so lovingly indulge Me?')

'Ah,' says the Lord, 'well done to you, for even though I am beyond the three gunas, My mind has been drawn to you. Your mind too has come to transcend the three gunas. Ah yes, I, the master of countless universes, entreat you: My full attention rests within My heart upon you. O Narsinh, know that what I say here is exactly true. Ah yes, Brahma, Shankar, Parvati, the Shrutis, and Sanaka and the other ancient ascetics and renunciants, as well as beings such as Sheshnag, Mahadev, and Shukdev, keep their contemplation fixed on Me. The liberation that people and ascetics seek to attain through meditation, knowledge, and the performance of rites, with mind, word, and deed — that very liberation I place under your command. To Me, you, Narsinh, are just like the gopis of Braj who perform love-devotion to Me; you are their equal, for you have performed My devotion with a pure, unblemished mind. Just as the petals of a flower are held tightly clasped together, so too I am, as it were, helplessly held, for you have held Me in your lap. Ah yes — in the play of the groves you delighted, reveling in pleasure like a bee, for in that play no one possessing the disposition of manhood can approach. From the very first, the true gopis of the Lord of Braj are there, and in that very state Narsinh too takes delight in the dust of their feet. In this play of Braj, who but Narsinh could please Me with love-devotion and lovingly indulge Me?'

Manhood is not found only in men — it is found in women as well. If a woman exerts her power and takes pride on the strength of her beauty, charm, skill, or status, that is "manhood" in a woman. In the same way, if a man sets aside his own ego and, through love and devotion, accepts refuge in the Lord, then that man is regarded as having "womanhood." Thus, whoever is free of ego is reckoned to have this womanhood. One who remains in the natural state (sahajavastha), that is, in the undistorted disposition, comes to attain love-devotion. Here, one who practices devotion while holding on to self-interest — on such a person the Lord bestows grace only to the extent of that self-interest. To show this sentiment, a morning kirtan (prabhatiyu) is presented, showing what the natural state (sahaj) of the gopis is, and what it teaches.

|| Prabhati || Kadakha Kedaro ||

_Te naarathi shun sukhiaa thaayes Shaamalaa, je naari naath kahi vinay karase.
Aafli aafli aavase aasare, jo rasiyaa tanu barad dharase. ||1||
Tehna dhiraj gun chaaturi aahaj lehese, ehavaa maanani maramnaa vachan varase.
Nirgun ati Shaamalo subah te me lahyo, nirakhavaa Krishnane nayan tarase. ||2||
Jeere meetra maahaaro sadaae prabhu avaraan tanu, muj vinaa e ras kon bharase.
Narsaiyaacho swaami jagat thamase sadaa, pan rooparas magan sang aanhaan j tharase._
(O Shyam, how could You find happiness through a woman who merely calls You her Lord and makes polite requests to You? Each such woman comes only for her own selfish refuge, even while claiming the vow of a true lover. She keeps only His patience and cleverness for her own purposes; such a proud woman's words fall full of hidden barbs. 'I have attained the utterly attributeless Shyam this very morning,' she boasts, while her eyes only long to gaze upon Krishna. Oh, my companion is always the Lord of others too — without me, who else could fill this love with such fullness? Narsaiya's Lord always keeps still amid the world, but engrossed in the joy of my form, He remains fixed right here.)

'O Krishna, how then will You find the joy of love-devotion through a self-interested, desire-laden gopi-woman? How will You expect the happiness of love, when such a woman, who humbly prays to You saying "my Lord, my Master," will suddenly, stumbling and falling, come to take Your refuge, presenting herself as one holding firm devotion to love for You? In this way, through the cleverness of her nature — her supposed patience being of little real worth — she will sigh and lament, and such a proud, honor-seeking woman will use words that strike at tender places. My eyes are eager to behold Lord Krishna. Ah yes — this Krishna is My eternal, deeply loving companion, bound to Me by an unbreakable tie; to everyone else He is the Supreme Lord and Master, and so, apart from Me, He may wander throughout the world — but His very body, absorbed in the joy of love-devotion, will settle and remain fixed right here, in Me.'

Only where the shock of the ego called manhood does not occur can the water of love-devotion remain stable. Thus Narsinh Mehta, having set aside manhood and taken on the surrendered devotion of sakhi-bhava (the companion's disposition), became worthy of beholding the Lord's raas. Such a state of being free from distortion is called the natural state (sahaj avastha). The Lord manifested from the midst of the gopis — that is, when the dualistic states such as honor and dishonor, pride and shame, joy and sorrow, come to an end, that is called "the midst" (madhya); and it was when the gopis reached this natural state that the Lord manifested from their midst. As for why He became hidden (antardhyan) — when a disturbance occurs in the state of love-devotion, love dissolves into waves and vanishes; that is called antardhyan. There the raas faltered, but Ram [the Lord] is unbroken, because the Lord's love-devotion never once ceases. When the endeavor of the paths of knowledge, action, and yoga meets with a shock, then all these — japa, tapa, and the like, the thieving "merchants" of ritual and duty — create obstruction in love-devotion. But such natural love-devotion, the gopi-natured devotion, comes about through the adoption of womanhood; yet giving up manhood is very difficult indeed.

Revered Yadunath Maharaj writes, in Lintiyu-57, page 6 (verso):

"The prabhatiyu that begins 'Dhanya tun dhanya tun,' spoken by Shri Hari, is of great importance. Bringing womanhood into a man's body is no small matter. When Mirabai went to meet Jiv Gosai, Jiv Gosai said, 'I do not look upon the face of a woman.' At this Mirabai said, 'What — is there still a man in Vrindavan?'"

Revered Yadunath, in Lintiyu No. 1, page 6, writes:

"The prabhatiyu that begins 'Dhanya tun dhanya tun,' spoken by Shri Hari, is of great importance. Bringing womanhood into a man's body is no small matter. When Mirabai went to meet Jiv Gosai, Jiv Gosai said, 'I do not look upon the face of a woman.' At this Mirabai said, 'What — is there still a man in Vrindavan?'"

Revered Yadunath, in Lintiyu No. 1, page 6, writes: "I was going to give some needed items to the students of the household in Vadodara. I was sitting on a bench on the platform at Miyagam, when a Muslim person came by, dressed in women's clothing; so, on some pretext, I struck up a conversation with him. From this I learned that in this whole path, throughout all of Hindustan, we are only three or four persons, and he lives in the guise of a sakhi."

Bhagwandas, the writer of the commentary on the Bhaktamal, lived in sakhi-form; his sakhi-name was Roopkala. He passed away a few years ago; he had been a school inspector at Mokri.

Just as Revered Yadunath saw a man dressed as a woman, I too once, on a bus, saw a man dressed in women's attire; he even had earrings in his ears. At that time I recalled the incident of Revered Yadunath, but I did not speak with him. In essence, there is a difference between merely going about with an outward appearance and living with the inward disposition. One may have a wish for womanhood, but that should not be about the difference of sex — rather, this "womanhood" should be for the sake of the disposition of non-attachment. After discussing the natural state (sahaj) of the gopis, it now turns to discuss Kabirji's natural state, saying:

_Kabir na kachhu kiya na kar shaka, na karane jog shareer.
Jo kachhu kiya so Hari kiya, taathe bhaya Kabir Kabir._
(Kabir says: I have done nothing, nor could I do anything, nor is this body fit to do anything. Whatever has been done, Hari alone has done it — and because of that, Kabir has come to be called Kabir.)

Das Kabir says: neither in the past have I been able to do anything, nor am I able to now, and neither is this body fit to do anything in the future. Whatever has been done at all, all of it the Lord Himself has done and caused to be done — and so it is Your own power alone that dwells within me.

_Kaayen vaachaa manasendriyair vaa buddhyaatmanaa vaa prakriteh svabhaavaat,
karomi yat tat sakalam parasmai Naaraayanaayeti samarthayaami._
(Whatever I do — with body, speech, mind and senses, intellect or self, or by the very nature of my constitution — all of it I dedicate wholly to the Supreme Narayana.)

'O Lord! Whatever I do at all times — with body and senses, with mind and intellect, or by my very nature — all of it has been offered and dedicated to You alone, for it is Yours.'

_Dehendriyothi man-buddhithi vaa svabhaavthi je karto sadaa hun,
Te sarva arpu tamane j devaah badhun tamaaru tamane samarpu.
Sattaa tamaari mujmaan vase chhe, tamo thaki hun karto janaank,
Karun, badhun hun tam-naath-kaaje, kashun na maaru, sadhalu tamaaru.
Badhun tamaaru, tamane samarpun, sveekaarasho naath! tamo tamaaru.
Swaami tamo, sevak hun tamaaro, shreepaadmaan vaas mane samarpo.
Swaami yathaa sevakni kanethi, prasann thaaye nijvastu paami,
Tevi j reete mujne dayaalo, jayaa tani drishti thaki nihaalo._
(Whatever I do, always, with body and senses, with mind and intellect, or by nature — all of it, O God, I offer to You; everything, whatever is Yours, I dedicate to You. Your power dwells within me; it is by You that I am made to act; whatever I do, I do it all for Your sake, O Lord; nothing is mine, all is Yours. Everything is Yours; I offer it to You — accept, O Lord, what is already Yours. You are the Master, I am Your servant; grant me a place at Your holy feet. Just as a master, receiving back his own possession from his servant, becomes pleased, so too, O Compassionate One, look upon me with that same gracious, victorious glance.)

_Jo kuchh kiya so Hari kiya, main kachhu kiya naahi.
Jo kahun kahi ki main kiya, tum hi the mujh maanhi._
(Whatever was done, Hari alone did it — I have done nothing at all. If I should ever say that I did something, it was You alone who dwelt within me.)

Das Kabir says: O Lord! All of it, everything, You Yourself have done. Even if I should say I have done something, it was You alone who were present within me as the capable power behind it.

_Meraa mujmen kachhun nahi, jo hai so teraa.
Teraa tujku sopte, kahaa lagegaa meraa._
(Nothing that is 'mine' truly exists in me; whatever there is, is Yours. In returning what is Yours to You, what of 'mine' shall be lost?)

_Kahaa lagegaa meraa, tamaarun tamaari paase.
(Trustee) saagreet sam chhun huy, aaptaan maaru shu jase.
Trikam saphal kar pheraa, paramaarath jhadapi sahi.
Jo hai so teraa, meraa mujmen kachhun nahin._
(What shall I lose? — what is Yours goes back to You. I am but like a custodian; what will I lose by giving it back? O Trikam, make this round of human birth fruitful, and swiftly grasp hold of the true purpose. Whatever exists is Yours; nothing that is 'mine' truly exists in me.)

Nothing at all has been accomplished by me, through myself; whatever strength, intellect, and so on I have is Yours alone. So then, what of mine will be lost in handing over what is Yours to You? What will I lose by giving back what is Yours? I am merely like a caretaker of Your possessions — what is lost by returning them? Trikamdas says: make this round of human birth of yours fruitful, and take hold of good deeds without delay. Whatever exists is Yours alone; there is nothing of mine in it.

Kabirji has shown the sentiment of the natural, detached disposition (sahaj tatasthapanu).

_Kabir sahaj sahaj sabkoy kahe, par sahaj na cheenhe koi.
Paancho raakhe parasten, sahaj kahaavai soi. ||1||_
(Kabir says: everyone speaks of 'sahaj, sahaj' [the natural state], but no one truly recognizes what sahaj is. He who keeps the five senses from touching their objects — he alone is truly called sahaj.)

Das Kabir says: everyone keeps talking about "sahaj, sahaj" [the undistorted state], but no one truly understands what should be called this natural non-attachment. One who restrains the five senses that go out toward sense-objects — that alone is called the natural state (sahajavastha), the state of detachment.

_Kabir sahaj sahaj sabkoy kahe, par sahaj na cheenhe koi.
Jo sahjai milai, sahaj kahaavai soi. ||2||_
(Kabir says: everyone speaks of 'sahaj, sahaj,' but no one truly recognizes what sahaj is. That which is attained naturally, with ease — that alone is truly called sahaj.)

Das Kabirji says: everyone keeps talking about sahaj, sahaj, but no one can say whether this "sahaj" is truly sahaj or not. Only that disposition of naturalness by adopting which one attains the Lord can be called the true natural disposition. Good disposition, good thought, and the like are what is called sahaj.

_Main dadhi mahi saate Jivana, paayo Padupati raay.
Shareer sonpu aapno, to leelaa kaise thaay. ||3||_
(In exchange for curd and buttermilk, O Jivana, I attained Padupati, the King. But if I surrender this body of mine entirely, then how could His playful sport ever take place?)

Maharaj Jivandasji says: in exchange for my craving to make use of curd and buttermilk-butter, I have taken the avatar of Yadupati Shri Krishna in order to obtain that buttermilk and butter. If I were to accept my own existence as non-different, in absolute oneness with the gopas and gopis — that is, if my body held complete unity with the gopas and gopis — then how could the delightful play of curd and butter ever take place?

Having spoken of the gopis' natural Prem-Lakshana Bhakti, now, in speaking of the natural Prem-Lakshana Bhakti of Kabirji and Narsinh Mehta, it is said that the Lord experiences love-devotion in two ways. An example of a king is given. A king enjoys the delight of love with his queens in the inner chambers of his palace, and also conducts the administration of the affairs and revenue of the kingdom in his court. In these two states, the delight of love is of a different kind in each. The king conducts the affairs of the court with the help of his minister, and it is the king who receives the results of this. But when the king has retired to rest within the inner chambers of his palace with his queens, there is no need there for a minister — there, the enjoyment of pleasure and delight can be given by none but the queens. When matters of the court arise, the king himself must leave the pleasure of the inner chambers to attend to them. And if there were no queens in the palace, then the affairs of those who come and go there could not be looked after by anyone else. Thus, for the king, there is no real difference between the pleasure enjoyed in these two places, the inner chambers and the court — both kinds of pleasure are just the same. The officer who administers the king's court, who tends the court of love-devotion, is Namdev-Kabirji; and the Master who enjoys love-devotion within the palace's inner chambers is the Lord Kripanath. And it is Narsinh Mehta who, within such a palace, is the giver of supreme pleasure. The natural Prem-Lakshana Bhakti of both Namdev-Kabir and Narsinh Mehta is one and the same. Narsinh Mehta is the one who tends to the Lord's love within the inner chambers. That is to say, Namdev-Kabir and Narsinh Mehta are both forms belonging to the Lord Himself; the two are not different — they are one and the same. The minister was said to be the one who tends to the affairs of the court, with no role in the bedchamber; whereas Narsinh Mehta is said to be the giver of delight in the bedchamber — yet the natural state of both is one. Looking at the Bhairav pad, relating to this bedchamber, which Kabir himself sang, it is shown that Kabir and Narsinh hold one and the same standing.

|| Bhairav ||

_Mai pahuaa vimal jash gadhzaa, charankamal Raajaa Raamji ke gaayaa.
Bhanat naat jet kachhu anamai, nai sadkaa le aavaa. ||tek||
Bheetar mahel podhe Kamalaapati, tahaan jaai main gaavaa.
Taathe prabhu meraa chamki jaagile, ko daas bandagi aavaa. ||1||_
(I have attained pure, radiant glory; I have sung of the lotus feet of King Ramji. Whatever I sing, [unclear], I have brought as a true offering. Within the palace, the Lotus-Lord (Kamalapati) lay resting; going there, I sang. At that, my Lord awoke with a start — [asking] which devotee has come in such devotion?)
